operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB: people=10 rows, gymnast=7 rows; original_values lists are short (<=10), so rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) draws with replacement from very few elements.
gymnast.Gymnast_ID is BOTH the single-column PK and an FK to people.People_ID: it is a PK (max_l0=inf) and an FK child (values copied from parent's final People_ID column).

FK child column == PK column: sample_fresh_primary_keys on gymnast drops duplicate Gymnast_IDs AFTER FK fill, so gymnast rows may shrink below chosen size; parent people.People_ID is filtered first (table order people before gymnast).
All declared types are INT/REAL -> Number fuzzer for every column; no String/Date/Time/Bool/Bit dispatch, no crash fallback, no text-stored dates.
REAL columns store real (9.725, 24.0, 1.71); INT columns store integer. No storage-class contradiction.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE, no composite keys, no self-FK, no dangling FK (parent people exists).
Mixed-case identifiers: Gymnast_ID, Floor_Exercise_Points, People_ID, Name, Hometown; must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
Name/Hometown contain non-ASCII (Súarez, Pérez, Quiñónez) and spaces; String fuzzer CHARSET is ASCII-only so fresh strings lose accents.
Age stored as REAL but semantically integer (24.0, 21.0); Height REAL ~1.7; Total_Points ~57-58 = sum of six ~9.5 events.
No views, indexes, or triggers in DDL; empty clone is just the two CREATE TABLEs.
people has 10 rows but only 7 are referenced by gymnast (Gymnast_ID samples 1,2,4,6,7); 3 people are unreferenced.
Vault_Points and Horizontal_Bar_Points have distinct=6 (one tie each); all other columns distinct=rows.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on every column: full range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from type args (INT/REAL have no args -> scale default), so fresh draws are huge (e.g. |v| up to 10^4) vs original ~9.5 or ~1.7.
Number list_max quirk (upper end overwritten by full-range max) means even 'list range' draws can exceed original max, producing implausible points >10 or heights >2.
Integer perturbation +-1/+-2 on Gymnast_ID/People_ID keeps IDs near originals but can collide -> PK dedup shrinks tables; FK fill copies parent's filtered IDs so referential integrity holds.
String fuzzer on Name/Hometown: 0.5 contaminate adds random ASCII suffix/prefix or drops chars; fresh strings are random a-zA-Z0-9() of length 0-20 -> implausible names, no accents.
p=0.2 default and whole-instance p=0 w.p. 0.3: 30% of instances are pure element-perturbation (near-original values), 70% mix fresh draws.
max_l0 cap (rng*30) on non-PK columns limits fresh draws, so many values are reused originals perturbed -> ties/duplicates appear where original had distinct=7.
Total_Points is generated independently of the six event columns -> sum(events) != Total_Points in generated rows (FN source for queries checking the sum).
Age/Height REAL get float perturbation +-0.01/+-0.02 -> 24.01, 1.69 etc.; plausible-ish but breaks exact equality with original constants.

Gymnast_ID as PK gets max_l0=inf -> many fresh huge IDs; as FK child it copies people.People_ID, so fresh huge IDs only survive if people also generated them (unlikely) -> gymnast mostly reuses parent IDs.
Small table sizes (choose_table_sizes: level0=1+30u, next x4 capped 2500) -> people ~1-31, gymnast ~4-124; often larger than original 10/7.
Queries with literal constants (e.g. Age=24, Total_Points>57) will miss because fresh values rarely equal originals; queries with joins on Gymnast_ID=People_ID survive via FK fill.
